mod5-theory-sdt.titleKo: 데시와 라이언(Deci & Ryan)의 자기결정이론: 자율성·유능감·관계성과 정보적 피드백 vs 통제적 언어
mod5-theory-sdt.titleEn: Self-Determination Theory (SDT): Basic Psychological Needs & Informational vs. Controlling Feedback

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Self-determination theory suggests that we all need to feel competent and capable in our interactions in the world, to have some choices and a sense of control over our lives, and to be connected to others—to belong to a social group. Notice that these are similar to early conceptions of basic needs for achievement (competence), power (autonomy and control), and affiliation (belonging and relatedness). Because different cultures have divergent conceptions of self, some psychologists have asked whether the needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness are universal. In a series of studies, Hyungshim Jang and her colleagues (2009) found that experiences of competence, autonomy, and relatedness were associated with satisfying learning experiences for Korean high school students, so even in a collectivistic culture, these needs may be important.
highlightQuotes: Notice that these are similar to early conceptions of basic needs for achievement (competence), power (autonomy and control), and affiliation (belonging and relatedness).
Because different cultures have divergent conceptions of self, some psychologists have asked whether the needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness are universal.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Cognitive evaluation theory: Suggests that events affect motivation through the individual’s perception of the events as controlling behavior or providing information. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 656)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 기본 심리욕구이론(Basic Psychological Needs Theory): 데시와 라이언(Deci & Ryan)의 자기결정이론(SDT)은 인간을 선천적 성장 지향성과 통합 욕구를 지닌 능동적 유기체로 규정하며, 사회·교실 환경이 3대 기본 심리욕구인 ① 자율성(Autonomy: 자신의 행동을 외적 강요가 아닌 스스로의 의지와 선택으로 조절한다는 인과소재의 내적 지각), ② 유능감(Competence: 환경과 효과적으로 상호작용하며 도전적 과제를 숙달하고 역량을 발휘한다는 효능감), ③ 관계성(Relatedness: 교사 및 또래와 조건 없이 안전하게 수용·연결되어 있다는 소속감)을 충족시켜 줄 때 내재적 동기와 심리적 안녕감이 극대화된다고 본다.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: INFORMATION AND CONTROL. Cognitive evaluation theory (Deci & Ryan, 2002) explains how students’ experiences such as being praised or criticized, reminded of deadlines, assigned grades, given choices, or lectured about rules can influence their intrinsic motivation by affecting their sense of self-determination and competence. According to this theory, all events have two aspects: controlling and informational. If an event is highly controlling—if it pressures students to act or feel a certain way—then students will experience less control, and their intrinsic motivation will be diminished. If, on the other hand, the event provides information that increases the students’ sense of competence, then intrinsic motivation will increase.
highlightQuotes: Cognitive evaluation theory (Deci & Ryan, 2002) explains how students’ experiences such as being praised or criticized, reminded of deadlines, assigned grades, given choices, or lectured about rules can influence their intrinsic motivation by affecting their sense of self-determination and competence.
According to this theory, all events have two aspects: controlling and informational.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 유기적 통합이론(Organismic Integration Theory)의 동기 내면화 연속체: 동기는 이분법적(내재 vs 외재)이 아니라 자기결정성의 수준에 따라 연속체 상에서 점진적으로 내면화(Internalization)된다: ① 무동기(Amotivation: 비인격적 인과소재, 행동-결과 유관성 상실) → ② 외적 조절(External Regulation: 외적 보상 획득·처벌 회피 목적의 타율적 수행) → ③ 부과된 조절(Introjected Regulation: 죄책감·수치심 회피나 조건부 자존심 유지를 위한 강박적 수행) → ④ 동일시 조절(Identified Regulation: 과제가 자신의 목표와 성장에 왜 중요한지 개인적 가치를 스스로 납득하여 수용) → ⑤ 통합된 조절(Integrated Regulation: 과제 가치가 개인의 핵심 정체성·가치관과 완전히 동화됨) → ⑥ 내재적 동기(Intrinsic Motivation: 앎의 즐거움과 호기심 자체를 위한 수행).

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: An extension of self-efficacy theory is self-determination theory, which is based on the idea that everyone has basic needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness to others. According to the theory, students will be motivated more intrinsically if these three needs are met as much as possible. A variety of strategies can assist teachers in doing so. As a practical matter, the strategies can encourage motivation that is more intrinsic to students, but usually not completely intrinsic.
highlightQuotes: An extension of self-efficacy theory is self-determination theory, which is based on the idea that everyone has basic needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness to others.
According to the theory, students will be motivated more intrinsically if these three needs are met as much as possible.

mod5-theory-achievement-goals-self-worth.titleKo: 성취목표이론(숙달목표 vs 수행접근·수행회피 목표)과 자기가치이론 및 자기구실 만들기(Self-Handicapping)
mod5-theory-achievement-goals-self-worth.titleEn: Achievement Goal Theory (Mastery vs. Performance-Approach/Avoidance) & Self-Worth Theory (Self-Handicapping)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: The most common distinction in research on students’ goals is between mastery goals (also called task goals or learning goals) and performance goals (also called ability goals or ego goals). The point of a mastery goal is to improve, to learn, no matter how awkward you appear. When students set mastery goals, the quality of their engagement in the task is higher—they are more invested, especially if they feel that they have choices and a sense of autonomy (Benita, Roth, & Deci, 2014). Students with mastery goals tend to seek challenges, persist when they encounter difficulties, and feel better about their work (Rolland, 2012). They focus on the task at hand and are not worried about how their performance “measures up” in comparison to others in the class. We often say that these people “get lost in their work.
highlightQuotes: The most common distinction in research on students’ goals is between mastery goals (also called task goals or learning goals) and performance goals (also called ability goals or ego goals).
The point of a mastery goal is to improve, to learn, no matter how awkward you appear.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Mastery goal: A personal intention to improve abilities and learn, no matter how performance suffers. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 660)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 성취목표이론(Achievement Goal Theory)의 2×2 매트릭스: 학습자가 학업 상황에서 유능감을 정의하는 준거(숙달 vs 수행)와 방향성(접근 vs 회피)에 따라 목표 지향성을 구분한다. ① 숙달접근목표(Mastery-Approach: 어제의 나보다 성장하고 과제를 깊이 이해·숙달하는 데 초점), ② 숙달회피목표(Mastery-Avoidance: 완벽주의적 기준에서 과거의 숙달 수준을 잃지 않으려는 초점), ③ 수행접근목표(Performance-Approach: 타인보다 우월한 등수와 능력을 과시하고 인정받는 데 초점), ④ 수행회피목표(Performance-Avoidance: 타인에게 무능해 보이거나 꼴찌가 되는 수치심을 피하는 데 초점).

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: GOALS IN SOCIAL CONTEXT. You have seen in other chapters that current thinking in educational psychology puts people in context. Goal orientation theory is no exception. The people in the situation socially construct the meaning of an activity, such as an assignment in a biology class; goals set for the activity will reflect the participants’ understanding of “what they are doing.” So, in a highly competitive classroom climate, students might be more likely to adopt performance goals. In contrast, in a supportive, learner-centered classroom, even a student with a lower sense of self-efficacy might be encouraged to aim for higher mastery goals.
highlightQuotes: The people in the situation socially construct the meaning of an activity, such as an assignment in a biology class; goals set for the activity will reflect the participants’ understanding of “what they are doing.” So, in a highly competitive classroom climate, students might be more likely to adopt performance goals.
In contrast, in a supportive, learner-centered classroom, even a student with a lower sense of self-efficacy might be encouraged to aim for higher mastery goals.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 드웩(Dweck)의 암묵적 지능신념(Implicit Theories of Intelligence): 지능과 능력이 타고나며 고정불변한다고 믿는 고정 마인드셋(Entity Theory) 학생은 어려운 과제에서의 오류를 '영구적 무능의 증거'로 해석하여 수행회피목표와 도전 회피에 빠진다. 반면 능력이 노력과 전략으로 확장된다고 믿는 성장 마인드셋(Incremental Theory) 학생은 실패를 '학습 전략을 수정하라는 유용한 피드백'으로 받아들이며 숙달접근목표를 견지한다.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Mastery goals tend to be associated with enjoyment of learning the material at hand, and in this sense represent an outcome that teachers often seek for students. By definition therefore they are a form of intrinsic motivation. As such mastery goals have been found to be better than performance goals at sustaining students’ interest in a subject. In one review of research about learning goals, for example, students with primarily mastery orientations toward a course they were taking not only tended to express greater interest in the course, but also continued to express interest well beyond the official end of the course, and to enroll in further courses in the same subject (Harackiewicz, et al., 2002; Wolters, 2004).
highlightQuotes: As such mastery goals have been found to be better than performance goals at sustaining students’ interest in a subject.
Mastery goals tend to be associated with enjoyment of learning the material at hand, and in this sense represent an outcome that teachers often seek for students.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 시험 전날 밤새 게임을 하거나 수행평가를 백지로 내며 '안 해서 그렇지 마음먹으면 잘해'라고 말하는 학생을 현장의 통념처럼 단순히 '게으르고 의지박약한 학생'으로 규정해 다그치거나 반성문을 쓰게 하면 개입은 반드시 역효과를 낳는다. 코빙턴(Covington)의 자기가치이론과 성취목표이론에 따르면, 이러한 자기구실 만들기(Self-Handicapping)는 게으름의 산물이 아니라 '최선을 다해 노력했는데도 성적이 안 나오면 내가…

mod5-theory-attribution-helplessness.titleKo: 와이너(Weiner)의 3차원 귀인이론(인과소재·안정성·통제가능성)과 학습된 무기력 및 재귀인 훈련
mod5-theory-attribution-helplessness.titleEn: Weiner's Three-Dimensional Attribution Theory, Learned Helplessness & Attribution Retraining

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Every cause for success or failure can be categorized on these three dimensions. For instance, luck is external (locus), unstable (stability), and uncontrollable (controllability). In attribution theory, ability is usually considered stable and uncontrollable, but incremental theorists (described earlier) would argue that ability is unstable and controllable. Weiner’s locus and controllability dimensions are closely related to Deci’s concept of locus of causality.
highlightQuotes: Weiner’s locus and controllability dimensions are closely related to Deci’s concept of locus of causality.
For instance, luck is external (locus), unstable (stability), and uncontrollable (controllability).
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Attribution theories: Descriptions of how individuals’ explanations, justifications, and excuses influence their motivation and behavior. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 655)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 와이너(Weiner)의 3차원 귀인 분류 체계: 학습자가 성취 결과(성공·실패)의 원인을 어떻게 해석하는지 3가지 차원으로 분석한다: ① 인과소재(Locus of Causality: 내적 vs 외적 — 자존감, 자부심 및 수치심과 직결), ② 안정성(Stability: 안정적 vs 불안정적 — 미래에 결과가 바뀔 수 있는지에 대한 성공 기대 Expectancy와 직결), ③ 통제가능성(Controllability: 통제 가능 vs 통제 불가능 — 죄책감·분노·동정 등 대인/자기 정서 반응 및 지속적 노력 의지와 직결).

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Weiner believes that these three dimensions have important implications for motivation because they affect expectancy and value. The stability dimension, for example, seems to be closely related to expectations about the future. If students attribute their failure to stable factors such as the difficulty of the subject or an unfair teacher, they will expect to keep failing in that subject or with that teacher. But if they attribute the outcome to unstable factors such as mood or luck, they can hope for better outcomes next time. The internal/external locus seems to be closely related to feelings of self-esteem. If success or failure is attributed to internal factors, success will lead to pride and increased motivation, whereas failure will diminish self-esteem.
highlightQuotes: Weiner believes that these three dimensions have important implications for motivation because they affect expectancy and value.
The stability dimension, for example, seems to be closely related to expectations about the future.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 학습된 무기력(Learned Helplessness)의 귀인 메커니즘: 반복된 실패를 경험한 학생이 실패 원인을 '타고난 지능·적성 부족(내적·안정적·통제불가능)'으로 귀인하고, 어쩌다 거둔 성공조차 '운이 좋았거나 문제가 쉬워서(외적·불안정적·통제불가능)'로 귀인하는 부적응적 도식이다. 이로 인해 미래 성공 기대가 완전히 붕괴(안정적 귀인)되고 수치심(내적 귀인)과 통제 불능감에 빠져 동기적·인지적·정서적 결손이 고착화된다.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Attributions vary in three underlying ways: locus, stability, and controllability. Locus of an attribution is the location (figuratively speaking) of the source of success or failure. If you attribute a top mark on a test to your ability, then the locus is internal; if you attribute the mark to the test’s having easy questions, then the locus is external. The stability of an attribution is its relative permanence. If you attribute the mark to your ability, then the source of success is relatively stable—by definition, ability is a relatively lasting quality. If you attribute a top mark to the effort you put in to studying, then the source of success is unstable—effort can vary and has to be renewed on each occasion or else it disappears. The controllability of an attribution is the extent to which the individual can influence it.
highlightQuotes: Attributions vary in three underlying ways: locus, stability, and controllability.
The controllability of an attribution is the extent to which the individual can influence it.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 학교 현장에서 학습된 무기력에 빠진 학생에게 가장 흔히 저지르는 선의의 실수는 '조금만 더 열심히 노력하면 너도 할 수 있어!'라며 무조건적인 '노력 귀인'을 강요하거나, 반대로 안쓰러운 마음에 너무 쉬운 과제만 주며 과잉 동정(Pity)을 베푸는 것이다. 와이너(Weiner)의 3차원 귀인이론 관점에서 볼 때, 과잉 동정은 교사가 학생의 실패를 '내적·안정적·통제불가능한 능력 결함'으로 단정했다는 강력한 비언어적 단서로 작동…

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 13 · Creating Learning Environments
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Here the teacher used empathetic listening to allow the student to find a solution. (As you can see, this approach relies heavily on paraphrasing.) By trying to hear the student and by avoiding the tendency to jump in too quickly with advice, solutions, criticisms, reprimands, or interrogations, the teacher keeps the communication lines open.
highlightQuotes: Here the teacher used empathetic listening to allow the student to find a solution.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Empathetic listening: Hearing the intent and emotions behind what another says and reflecting them back by paraphrasing. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 657)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 고든(Gordon)의 문제 소유권(Problem Ownership) 판별 원리: 교사효율성훈련(TET)의 핵심 출발점은 갈등이나 부적응 행동 상황에서 '현재 누구의 정당한 욕구가 직접 좌절되어 부정적 감정을 겪고 있는가'를 기준으로 ① 학생 소유 문제(학생 자신의 불안·소외·진로 고민), ② 교사 소유 문제(학생의 행동이 교사의 수업 진행이나 타 학생의 안전·학습권을 실질적으로 침해), ③ 양측 욕구 충돌 영역을 엄밀히 변별하는 것이다.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 13 · Creating Learning Environments
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: “I” MESSAGES. T. Gordon (1981) recommends sending an “I” message to intervene and change a student’s behavior. Basically, this means telling a student in a straightforward, assertive, and nonjudgmental way what she or he is doing, how it affects you as a teacher, and how you feel about it. The student is then free to change voluntarily, and often does so.
highlightQuotes: Gordon (1981) recommends sending an “I” message to intervene and change a student’s behavior.
Basically, this means telling a student in a straightforward, assertive, and nonjudgmental way what she or he is doing, how it affects you as a teacher, and how you feel about it.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 학생 소유 문제와 의사소통 걸림돌(12 Roadblocks) 배제 및 적극적 경청(Active Listening): 학생이 문제를 소유했을 때 교사가 명령·훈계·성급한 충고·논리적 설득·심문·가벼운 위안 같은 '의사소통 걸림돌(Communication Roadblocks)'을 사용하면 학생은 방어적으로 입을 닫거나 교사에게 의존하게 된다. 대신 학생의 발화 이면에 담긴 핵심 감정과 의미를 정확히 해독하여 비심판적 언어로 되비추어 주는 적극적 경청(Active Listening)을 통해 정서적 카타르시스와 자기주도적 문제해결력을 촉진한다.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 7 · Classroom Management and the Learning Environment
excerpts.sectionHeading: Chapter 7 · Classroom Management and the Learning Environment
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: In a widely cited approach to conflict resolution called Teacher Effectiveness Training, the educator Thomas Gordon describes this challenge as an issue of problem ownership, or deciding whose problem a behavior or conflict it really is (Gordon, 2003). The “owner” of the problem is the primary person who is troubled or bothered by it. The owner can be the student committing the behavior, the teacher, or another student who merely happens to see the behavior. Since the owner of a problem needs to take primary responsibility for solving it, identifying ownership makes a difference in how to deal with the behavior or problem effectively.
highlightQuotes: In a widely cited approach to conflict resolution called Teacher Effectiveness Training, the educator Thomas Gordon describes this challenge as an issue of problem ownership, or deciding whose problem a behavior or conflict it really is (Gordon, 2003).
The “owner” of the problem is the primary person who is troubled or bothered by it.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 학교 현장에서 학급 갈등이나 관계적 공격성(Relational Aggression: 은밀한 소외, 단톡방 따돌림, 루머 유포)을 다룰 때 흔히 범하는 두 가지 오류는 첫째, 고든의 '문제 소유권'을 혼동하여 상처 입은 피해 학생에게 성급한 충고나 심문(의사소통 걸림돌)을 쏟아붓고 수업 방해 학생에게는 인격 비난적 너-전달법(또는 '나는 네가 참 한심하다고 느낀다'식의 위장된 나-전달법)을 구사하는 것이며, 둘째, 응보적 정의에…

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Self-determination theory suggests that we all need to feel competent and capable in our interactions in the world, to have some choices and a sense of control over our lives, and to be connected to others—to belong to a social group. Notice that these are similar to early conceptions of basic needs for achievement (competence), power (autonomy and control), and affiliation (belonging and relatedness). Because different cultures have divergent conceptions of self, some psychologists have asked whether the needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness are universal. In a series of studies, Hyungshim Jang and her colleagues (2009) found that experiences of competence, autonomy, and relatedness were associated with satisfying learning experiences for Korean high school students, so even in a collectivistic culture, these needs may be important.
highlightQuotes: Notice that these are similar to early conceptions of basic needs for achievement (competence), power (autonomy and control), and affiliation (belonging and relatedness).
Because different cultures have divergent conceptions of self, some psychologists have asked whether the needs for competence, autonomy, and relatedness are universal.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Need for autonomy: The desire to have our own wishes, rather than external rewards or pressures, determine our actions. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 660)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 데시와 라이언(Deci & Ryan)이 제시한 동기 이론으로, 인간이 자율성(자기결정감), 유능감(과제 숙달 효능감), 관계성(안전한 소속감과 수용)의 3대 기본 심리욕구를 충족받을 때 내재적 동기와 자율적 내면화가 촉진된다는 이론. (현장 적용: 독서 과제 수행 시 도서 목록과 결과물 표현 방식(만화, 발표, 서평 중 택1)에 선택권을 부여(자율성)하고, 수준별 읽기 비계(유능감)와 모둠의 따뜻한 경청 규칙(관계성)을 결합한다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: An extension of self-efficacy theory is self-determination theory, which is based on the idea that everyone has basic needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness to others. According to the theory, students will be motivated more intrinsically if these three needs are met as much as possible. A variety of strategies can assist teachers in doing so. As a practical matter, the strategies can encourage motivation that is more intrinsic to students, but usually not completely intrinsic.
highlightQuotes: An extension of self-efficacy theory is self-determination theory, which is based on the idea that everyone has basic needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness to others.
According to the theory, students will be motivated more intrinsically if these three needs are met as much as possible.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 데시와 라이언(Deci & Ryan)이 제시한 동기 이론으로, 인간이 자율성(자기결정감), 유능감(과제 숙달 효능감), 관계성(안전한 소속감과 수용)의 3대 기본 심리욕구를 충족받을 때 내재적 동기와 자율적 내면화가 촉진된다는 이론.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: INFORMATION AND CONTROL. Cognitive evaluation theory (Deci & Ryan, 2002) explains how students’ experiences such as being praised or criticized, reminded of deadlines, assigned grades, given choices, or lectured about rules can influence their intrinsic motivation by affecting their sense of self-determination and competence. According to this theory, all events have two aspects: controlling and informational. If an event is highly controlling—if it pressures students to act or feel a certain way—then students will experience less control, and their intrinsic motivation will be diminished. If, on the other hand, the event provides information that increases the students’ sense of competence, then intrinsic motivation will increase.
highlightQuotes: According to this theory, all events have two aspects: controlling and informational.

Cognitive evaluation theory (Deci & Ryan, 2002) explains how students’ experiences such as being praised or criticized, reminded of deadlines, assigned grades, given choices, or lectured about rules can influence their intrinsic motivation by affecting their sense of self-determination and competence.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Cognitive evaluation theory: Suggests that events affect motivation through the individual’s perception of the events as controlling behavior or providing information. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 656)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 인지평가이론에 따라 강압적 당위('~해야만 해', 감시·비교)를 담은 통제적 언어는 학생의 자율성을 침해해 내재적 동기를 꺾는 반면, 구체적 성장과 전략 개선점을 알려주는 정보적 피드백은 유능감을 높여 내재적 동기를 증진시킨다. (현장 적용: '숙제 안 해오면 벌점이다(통제적 언어)' 대신 '지난번보다 문단 핵심어 찾기가 훨씬 정확해졌네. 여기에 근거 문장 1개만 더 연결하면 글의 설득력이 배가 될 거야(정보적 피드백)'라고 전달한다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Table 16 summarizes and gives examples of the various levels and their effects on motivation. By assuming that motivation is often a mix of the intrinsic and extrinsic, the job of the teacher becomes more realistic; the job is not to expect purely intrinsic motivation from students all the time, but simply to arrange and encourage motivations that are as intrinsic as possible. To do this, the teacher needs to support students’ basic needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness.
highlightQuotes: To do this, the teacher needs to support students’ basic needs for autonomy, competence, and relatedness.

By assuming that motivation is often a mix of the intrinsic and extrinsic, the job of the teacher becomes more realistic; the job is not to expect purely intrinsic motivation from students all the time, but simply to arrange and encourage motivations that are as intrinsic as possible.

mod5-fc-internalization-continuum.titleEn: Continuum of Extrinsic Motivation Internalization (External, Introjected, Identified, Integrated)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: One is that our activities fall along a continuum from fully self-determined (intrinsic motivation) to fully determined by others (extrinsic motivation). Four types of extrinsic motivation are based on level of internal drive to engage in the activity. Starting with the most extrinsic, these four types are external regulation (completely controlled by outside consequences), introjected regulation (engaging in the task to avoid guilt or negative self-perceptions), identification (participating despite lack of interest because it serves a larger goal that is personally motivating), and integrated regulation (participating in a task because it is both interesting and has extrinsic reward value).
highlightQuotes: One is that our activities fall along a continuum from fully self-determined (intrinsic motivation) to fully determined by others (extrinsic motivation).
Four types of extrinsic motivation are based on level of internal drive to engage in the activity.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Extrinsic motivation: Motivation created by external factors such as rewards and punishments. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 658)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 외재적 동기가 자율성의 정도에 따라 외적 조절(보상·처벌) → 부과된 조절(죄책감·불안 회피, 자존심) → 동일시 조절(가치와 중요성 인정) → 통합된 조절(자기 정체성과 통합)로 점차 내면화되는 단계. (현장 적용: 단순히 부모에게 혼나지 않으려 공부하던(외적·부과된 조절) 학생에게 해당 교과의 학습 이유와 자신의 진로 가치를 연결해 주어 스스로 필요성을 느끼는 '동일시 조절'로 이행하도록 돕는다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Psychologists who study self-efficacy have identified four major sources of self-efficacy beliefs (Pajares & Schunk, 2001, 2002). In order of importance they are (1) prior experiences of mastering tasks, (2) watching others’ mastering tasks, (3) messages or “persuasion” from others, and (4) emotions related to stress and discomfort. Fortunately the first three can be influenced by teachers directly, and even the fourth can sometimes be influenced indirectly by appropriate interpretive comments from the teacher or others.
highlightQuotes: Psychologists who study self-efficacy have identified four major sources of self-efficacy beliefs (Pajares & Schunk, 2001, 2002).
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 외재적 동기가 자율성의 정도에 따라 외적 조절(보상·처벌) → 부과된 조절(죄책감·불안 회피, 자존심) → 동일시 조절(가치와 중요성 인정) → 통합된 조절(자기 정체성과 통합)로 점차 내면화되는 단계.

mod5-fc-mastery-performance-goals.titleEn: Mastery Goal vs. Performance-Approach / Performance-Avoidance Goal

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Two final cautions—performance-approach goals can turn into performance-avoidance goals if students are not successful in looking smart or winning. The path might lead from performance approach (trying to win), to performance avoidance (saving face and trying not to look dumb), to learned helplessness (I give up!). So teachers are wise to avoid trying to motivate using competition and social comparisons (Brophy, 2005). In addition, performance-approach and performance-avoidance goals tend to be moderately correlated, so students may pursue both types of performance goals at once (Linnenbrink-Garcia et al., 2012).
highlightQuotes: In addition, performance-approach and performance-avoidance goals tend to be moderately correlated, so students may pursue both types of performance goals at once (Linnenbrink-Garcia et al., 2012).
Two final cautions—performance-approach goals can turn into performance-avoidance goals if students are not successful in looking smart or winning.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Mastery goal: A personal intention to improve abilities and learn, no matter how performance suffers. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 660)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 과제 자체의 이해와 어제의 나보다 성장하는 것에 가치를 두는 숙달목표와 달리, 수행접근목표는 타인보다 우월한 성적을 증명하려 하고, 수행회피목표는 무능해 보이거나 실패하는 수치심을 피하는 데 급급해 부적응적 회피를 낳는다. (현장 적용: 성적순 좌석 배치나 공개 석차 게시를 폐지하고, 학생 각자의 이전 단원 대비 향상도와 오류 수정 과정을 인정하는 숙달목표 중심 학급 구조(TARGET 모형)를 구축한다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: What kinds of achievement goals do students hold? Imagine three individuals, Maria, Sara, and Lindsay, who are taking algebra together. Maria’s main concern is to learn the material as well as possible because she finds it interesting and because she believes it will be useful to her in later courses, perhaps at university. Hers is a mastery goal because she wants primarily to learn or master the material. Sara, however, is concerned less about algebra than about getting top marks on the exams and in the course. Hers is a performance goal because she is focused primarily on looking successful; learning algebra is merely a vehicle for performing well in the eyes of peers and teachers. Lindsay, for her part, is primarily concerned about avoiding a poor or failing mark.
highlightQuotes: Hers is a mastery goal because she wants primarily to learn or master the material.
Hers is a performance goal because she is focused primarily on looking successful; learning algebra is merely a vehicle for performing well in the eyes of peers and teachers.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 과제 자체의 이해와 어제의 나보다 성장하는 것에 가치를 두는 숙달목표와 달리, 수행접근목표는 타인보다 우월한 성적을 증명하려 하고, 수행회피목표는 무능해 보이거나 실패하는 수치심을 피하는 데 급급해 부적응적 회피를 낳는다.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Failure-avoiding students tend to hold an entity (fixed) view of ability, so they set performance goals. They lack a strong sense of their own competence and self-worth separate from their performance. In other words, they feel only as smart as their last test grade, so they never develop a solid sense of self-efficacy. To feel competent, they must protect themselves (and their self-worth) from failure. If they have been generally successful, they may seek to avoid failure like Safe Sumey, simply by taking few risks and “sticking with what they know.” If, on the other hand, they have experienced a good bit of failure, then they, like Defensive Daleesha, may adopt self-defeating strategies such as feeble efforts, setting very low or ridiculously high goals, or claiming not to care.
highlightQuotes: Failure-avoiding students tend to hold an entity (fixed) view of ability, so they set performance goals.
To feel competent, they must protect themselves (and their self-worth) from failure.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Self-handicapping: Students may engage in behavior that blocks their own success in order to avoid testing their true ability. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 663)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 코빙턴(Covington)의 이론으로, 실패했을 때 '능력이 부족한 사람'으로 판명되어 자기가치가 훼손되는 것을 막기 위해 시험 전날 일부러 공부를 안 하거나 미루는 등 실패의 외적 핑곗거리를 스스로 만드는 방어적 전략. (현장 적용: 시험 전날 밤새 게임을 하고 와서 '어제 공부 하나도 안 해서 망쳤어'라고 말하는 학생의 이면에 있는 무능 노출 공포를 공감하고, 성적과 인간적 자기가치를 분리하는 상담을 진행한다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Third, teachers need to remember that ability—usually considered a relatively stable factor—often actually changes incrementally over the long term. Recognizing this fact is one of the best ways to bring about actual increases in students’ abilities (Blackwell, Trzniewski, & Dweck, 2007; Schunk, Pintrich, & Meese, 2008). A middle- years student might play the trumpet in the school band at a high level of ability, but this ability actually reflects a lot of previous effort and a gradual increase in ability.
highlightQuotes: A middle- years student might play the trumpet in the school band at a high level of ability, but this ability actually reflects a lot of previous effort and a gradual increase in ability.
Third, teachers need to remember that ability—usually considered a relatively stable factor—often actually changes incrementally over the long term.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 코빙턴(Covington)의 이론으로, 실패했을 때 '능력이 부족한 사람'으로 판명되어 자기가치가 훼손되는 것을 막기 위해 시험 전날 일부러 공부를 안 하거나 미루는 등 실패의 외적 핑곗거리를 스스로 만드는 방어적 전략.

mod5-fc-weiner-attribution.titleEn: Weiner's Three-Dimensional Attribution Theory (Locus, Stability, Controllability)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Every cause for success or failure can be categorized on these three dimensions. For instance, luck is external (locus), unstable (stability), and uncontrollable (controllability). In attribution theory, ability is usually considered stable and uncontrollable, but incremental theorists (described earlier) would argue that ability is unstable and controllable. Weiner’s locus and controllability dimensions are closely related to Deci’s concept of locus of causality.
highlightQuotes: For instance, luck is external (locus), unstable (stability), and uncontrollable (controllability).
Weiner’s locus and controllability dimensions are closely related to Deci’s concept of locus of causality.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Attribution theories: Descriptions of how individuals’ explanations, justifications, and excuses influence their motivation and behavior. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 655)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 성공과 실패의 원인을 인과소재(내적/외적), 안정성(안정적/불안정적), 통제가능성(통제 가능/불가능)의 3차원으로 분석하여 후속 정서(자부심·수치심·분노·동정)와 미래 성공 기대, 성취 행동을 설명하는 이론. (현장 적용: 시험 실패를 '타고난 수학 머리 부족(내적·안정적·통제불가능)'으로 귀인하는 학생에게 '이번 단원의 오답 노트 인출 전략 부족(내적·불안정적·통제가능)'으로 재귀인시켜 미래 성공 기대를 회복시킨다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Attributions vary in three underlying ways: locus, stability, and controllability. Locus of an attribution is the location (figuratively speaking) of the source of success or failure. If you attribute a top mark on a test to your ability, then the locus is internal; if you attribute the mark to the test’s having easy questions, then the locus is external. The stability of an attribution is its relative permanence. If you attribute the mark to your ability, then the source of success is relatively stable—by definition, ability is a relatively lasting quality. If you attribute a top mark to the effort you put in to studying, then the source of success is unstable—effort can vary and has to be renewed on each occasion or else it disappears. The controllability of an attribution is the extent to which the individual can influence it.
highlightQuotes: Attributions vary in three underlying ways: locus, stability, and controllability.
If you attribute a top mark on a test to your ability, then the locus is internal; if you attribute the mark to the test’s having easy questions, then the locus is external.
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 성공과 실패의 원인을 인과소재(내적/외적), 안정성(안정적/불안정적), 통제가능성(통제 가능/불가능)의 3차원으로 분석하여 후속 정서(자부심·수치심·분노·동정)와 미래 성공 기대, 성취 행동을 설명하는 이론.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 12 · Motivation In Learning And Teaching
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: LEARNED HELPLESSNESS. When people come to believe that the events and outcomes in their lives are mostly uncontrollable, they have developed learned helplessness (Seligman, 1975). To understand the power of learned helplessness, consider this classic experiment (Hiroto & Seligman, 1975): Subjects received either solvable or unsolvable puzzles. In the next phase of the experiment, all subjects were given a series of solvable puzzles. The subjects who struggled with unsolvable puzzles in the first phase of the experiment usually solved significantly fewer puzzles in the second phase. They had learned that they could not control the outcome, so why even try?
highlightQuotes: When people come to believe that the events and outcomes in their lives are mostly uncontrollable, they have developed learned helplessness (Seligman, 1975).
To understand the power of learned helplessness, consider this classic experiment (Hiroto & Seligman, 1975): Subjects received either solvable or unsolvable puzzles.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: Learned helplessness: The expectation, based on previous experiences with a lack of control, that all of one’s efforts will lead to failure. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 659)
excerpts.koreanContextGuide: 반복된 실패를 내적·안정적·통제불가능한 능력 부족 탓으로 귀인하여 아무리 노력해도 결과를 바꿀 수 없다고 체념하는 상태가 학습된 무기력이며, 이를 통제 가능한 전략과 노력 귀인으로 교정하는 개입이 재귀인 훈련이다. (현장 적용: 무기력한 학생에게 무조건 '열심히 노력해'라고 강요하면 재실패 시 능력 부족 귀인이 더 고착되므로, 반드시 달성 가능한 소단계 과제와 구체적 풀이 전략을 함께 제공하며 재귀인 훈련을 실시한다.)

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 6 · Student Motivation
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: If a person’s sense of self-efficacy is very low, he or she can develop learned helplessness, a perception of complete lack of control in mastering a task. The attitude is similar to depression, a pervasive feeling of apathy and a belief that effort makes no difference and does not lead to success. Learned helplessness was originally studied from the behaviorist perspective of classical and operant conditioning by the psychologist Martin Seligman (1995). The studies used a somewhat “gloomy” experimental procedure in which an animal, such as a rat or a dog, was repeatedly shocked in a cage in a way that prevented the animal from escaping the shocks. In a later phase of the procedure, conditions were changed so that the animal could avoid the shocks by merely moving from one side of the cage to the other. Yet frequently they did not bother to do so!
highlightQuotes: If a person’s sense of self-efficacy is very low, he or she can develop learned helplessness, a perception of complete lack of control in mastering a task.
Learned helplessness was originally studied from the behaviorist perspective of classical and operant conditioning by the psychologist Martin Seligman (1995).

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 13 · Creating Learning Environments
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: As a teacher, you may find many student behaviors unacceptable, unpleasant, or troubling. It is often difficult to stand back from these problems, take an objective look, and decide on an appropriate response. According to Thomas Gordon (1981), the key to good teacher–student relationships is determining why you are troubled by a particular behavior and who “owns” the problem. The answer to these questions is critical. If it is really the student’s problem, the teacher must become a counselor and supporter, helping the student find his or her own solution. But if the teacher “owns” the problem, it is the teacher’s responsibility to find a solution through problem solving with the student.
highlightQuotes: According to Thomas Gordon (1981), the key to good teacher–student relationships is determining why you are troubled by a particular behavior and who “owns” the problem.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 7 · Classroom Management and the Learning Environment
excerpts.sectionHeading: Chapter 7 · Classroom Management and the Learning Environment
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: Diagnosing accurately who really has a problem with a behavior—who “owns” it—is helped by a number of strategies. One is active listening—attending carefully to all aspects of what a student says and attempting to understand or empathize as fully as possible, even if you do not agree with what is being said (Cooper & Simonds, 2003). Active listening involves asking questions in order continually to check your understanding. It also involves encouraging the student to elaborate on his or her remarks, and paraphrasing and summarizing what the student says in order to check your perceptions of what is said. It is important not to move too fast toward solving the problem with advice, instructions, or scolding, even if these are responses that you might, as a teacher, feel responsible for making.

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 13 · Creating Learning Environments
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: CONFRONTATIONS AND NEGOTIATIONS. If “I” messages or assertive responses fail and a student persists in misbehaving, teacher and student are in a conflict. Several pitfalls now loom. The two individuals become less able to perceive each other’s behavior accurately. Research has shown that the more angry you get with another person, the more you see the other as the villain and yourself as an innocent victim. Because you feel the other person is in the wrong, and he or she feels just as strongly that the conflict is all your fault, very little mutual trust is possible. A cooperative solution to the problem is almost impossible. In fact, by the time the discussion has gone on a few minutes, the original problem is lost in a sea of charges, countercharges, and self-defense (Baron & Byrne, 2003).
highlightQuotes: If “I” messages or assertive responses fail and a student persists in misbehaving, teacher and student are in a conflict.
excerpts.glossaryEntry: “I” message: Clear, nonaccusatory statement of how something is affecting you. (Woolfolk Glossary, p. 659)

excerpts.sectionHeading: Chapter 7 · Classroom Management and the Learning Environment
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: • The comments should emphasize I-messages (Gordon, 1981), which are comments that focus on how the problem behavior is affecting the teacher’s ability to teach, as well as how the behavior makes the teacher feel. They are distinct from you-messages, which focus on evaluating the mistake or problem which the student has created. An I-message might be, “Your talking is making it hard for me to remember what I’m trying to say.” A you-message might be, “Your talking is rude.”

excerpts.chapterLabel: Chapter 13 · Creating Learning Environments
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: RESTORATIVE JUSTICE. Restorative justice focuses on righting the wrongs suffered when conflicts go badly (D. W. Johnson & Johnson, 2013). Probably the most famous example of restorative justice was the National Truth and Reconciliation Commission in South Africa, where injured parties described the injustices they had experienced and sometimes faced those who had harmed them. In classrooms, the goals of restorative justice look to the past and the future: re-establish cooperation in the classroom community by resolving past conflicts and create conditions for long-term future cooperation. The process must be voluntary. The participants in the conflict meet with a facilitator (often the teacher) and sometimes members of their family.

excerpts.sectionHeading: Chapter 8 · The Nature of Classroom Communication
excerpts.verbatimExcerpt: • If conflicts arise between students or between a student and teacher, encourage respectful communication as explicitly as you can. Some communication strategies about conflict resolution were described in Chapter 7 and are helpful in this regard: identifying true problem ownership, listening actively, assertive (not aggressive) I-messages, and negotiation.
